D.treatment: MZI QuILT with guided simulation and questions

O.outcome_detail: Understanding that a path detector collapses the photon state and destroys interference

cells.quote: On the pretest, 28% of the students incorrectly claimed that adding a detector in the L path would not change anything or would only cause fewer photons arrive at detectors D1 and D2 because some photons are absorbed. These students struggled with the fact that the detector in the L path acts as a measurement device and will collapse the state of the photons not absorbed by it to the U path state. After working on the QuILT, the difficulty with the effect of an additional detector placed in the L path of the MZI was eliminated (see Table 1).
cells.note: Table 1 reports the difficulty declining from 28% on the pretest to 0% on the posttest; Table 2 reports Q5 scores increasing from 56% to 100%. The study does not state learners' prior knowledge or the QuILT's duration, and its pretest-posttest design does not match a specified design category.

cells.quote: On the pretest, 56% of students incorrectly claimed that removing or inserting BS2 will not change the probability of the photon arriving at D1 and D2 . In the QuILT, students learn ed that if BS2 is present, it evolves the state of the photon such that both paths can be projected by each detector and interference is displayed at D1 and D2.
